name: Catalog of Termination Proof Routes and Six-Stage Ascent Profiles
description: Classifies W1 licensed escapes, FBI catalogs and generic DP methods with six-step ascent profiles. Six canonical witnesses partition into W1 and W2 with permitted imports.

program.name: Certificates and Confession
program.summary: A construction method adds comparison data and verifies the original relation; a confession method transforms the problem, omits a coordinate and transports the result through a soundness theorem. The confession routes for the kernel share the canonical dependency-pair rank, the typed external-license schemas are related by quasi-functors with one irreversible license stage, and licensed transactions compose with ledgers while no rule recovers the composite semantic profile from the factor capabilities alone.

oneLine: Six named construction packages are assigned by definition four to W1 imports and two to W2 transformed calls, and each carries proved evidence: the multiset path order and a polynomial interpretation orient the KO7 step, the full-duplicating benchmark member has a decreasing rank and no additive measure, and the dependency-pair projection decreases across the duplicating rule.
summary: The objects are construction routes W0 (direct measures), W1 (imported orders and ranks) and W2 (transformed calls) with six named route packages, finite catalogs of FBI methods with forward, backward and bidirectional instantiations, generic dependency-pair and semantic methods, and six-stage ascent profiles compared with the dependency-pair profile. The six packages are assigned four to W1 and two to W2 by the definition of the route function, and their evidence is proved: the multiset path order and the polynomial interpretation orient every KO7 root step, the polynomial interpretation is neither transparent at the base nor additive nor affine in its arguments, the full-duplicating benchmark member has a decreasing natural-number rank and a decreasing transformed-call rank and no additive measure, and the dependency-pair projection decreases across the duplicating rule. Seven W1 method rows are supported by permitted imports, each W1 row realizes its six-step ascent profile, and a construction response and a forgetting record on one schema never share a rank. The FBI, generic dependency-pair and semantic catalogs assign closure statuses by definition and every listed method lies in its finite list; the external TTT2 run is recorded with status MAYBE, every semantic method is classified as a W1 licensed escape by definition, and the six dependency-pair and three semantic methods give nine types. Realizing the six-step shape is equivalent to a stagewise realization, and every profile compatible with the dependency-pair profile shares its family and stagewise shape. On KO7 no orienter from the representable direct barrier classes orients the root relation, the root relation and the dependency-pair relation are well founded, and the benchmark contract, which excludes the two lower levels of the tower ko7Tower by definition, holds at the transformed-call level; the projection theorem from the imported-whole level assumes a level the contract excludes and returns the transformed-call proof without using its hypothesis. Comparison hom-sets between ascent profiles are subsingletons, the Godel checker ascent maps to the quotation ascent while the orientation and quotation ascents admit no map either way although all three realize the six-step shape, and the Godel-1931 profile is a stipulated all-True profile, so its compatibility with the dependency-pair profile concerns stage shapes only.
boundary: For the benchmark recursion family a direct W0 route is an additive measure, and the full-duplicating member has none while it has a decreasing natural-number rank and a decreasing rank on transformed calls; for KO7, no orienter from the representable direct barrier classes orients the root relation, while the multiset path order and a non-transparent, non-affine polynomial interpretation do. The imported-whole and transformed-call levels of the tower ko7Tower carry the well-foundedness of the KO7 root relation and of the dependency-pair relation, and the benchmark contract holds at the transformed-call level because its definition excludes the two lower levels. Catalog closure statuses, the W1 classification of semantic methods and the MAYBE status of the external TTT2 run are recorded labels, and comparison maps between ascent profiles exist at the shape layer while the orientation and quotation ascents admit no ascent homomorphism either way.

conclusions.statement: For every canonical witness, if it satisfies the W1 predicate then its route is W1 with a W1 success payload, and if it satisfies the W2 predicate then its route is W2 with a W2 success payload; the W1 predicate holds exactly when the route equals W1 and the W2 predicate holds exactly when the route equals W2, and the bundled final catalog with certificate, exactness, audit, partition, no-overlap and payload consistency holds.

For every canonical witness w, w belongs to the six-element list exactly when w is one of the six constructors; the list is duplicate-free with length 6 and every witness belongs to it, and for every w belonging to the list there is a W1 or W2 payload and the route is not W0, with the combined exactness and audit catalogs holding.

Each of the four canonical W1 packages has its stated import class with permitted import; the imported-whole W1 route is not W0 with fullDuplicating having an imported-whole witness and no direct witness; the nonlinear polynomial witness is not transparent at base and is neither additive with a constant nor affine in its arguments.

For every W2 success S, S yields a permitted transform for its transform class and target and yields a transformed-call witness for its target; both canonical duplicating and linear values satisfy the target, route, permitted-transform and witness conjunctions; the duplicating W2 route is not W0 with a transformed-call witness for fullDuplicating and no direct witness for fullDuplicating.

For every W1 method row, row support holds with W1 route and licensed-escape W1 status inventoried in the catalog; for every supported row there is a permitted import of its assigned class; for every W1 row the route differs from W0 and from W2.

For every W1 method row, its six-step ascent profile is realized; every W1 row has a permitted import, licensed-escape W1 status, and routes distinct from W0 and W2 with construction and confession ranks exclusive; for every construction response and forgetting witness on the same schema with equal ranks, False follows.

For every FBI method, its closure status lies in the finite closure-status list and final-catalog coverage holds; every final catalog row is supported with exact route and status projections; the final route-status catalog is realized and the direction-indexed route-status catalog is total over FBI methods.
The external TTT2 FBI status is recorded as maybe in the constant fbiExternalTTT2Status and differs from certifiedYes; both facts read that recorded constant.

For every generic DP method, it lies in the six-member list and its classification lies in the canonical status list; for every boundary class, grammar classification of its embedding matches the boundary status table, and the embedding from boundary classes to grammar methods is injective.

For every generic DP boundary class, its support payload holds with catalog membership and status table, and its boundary route is not some W0; if a class route equaled some W0 then False follows, with the boundary certificate with W0 exclusion holding.

For every semantic class, support holds with exact route and status and catalog membership; the imported method status equals licensed escape at W1 and its route differs from some W0; universal DP plus semantic coverage and classification hold with 6 plus 3 equal to 9.

A profile realizes the six-step shape exactly if it has a stagewise realization; every profile compatible with DP realizes the six-step shape with the DP family and is stagewise equivalent to DP, and so do the benchmark-transport profile and the synthetic Godel-1931 profile with all six stages stipulated True.

The contracted benchmark tower has kappa at most the transformed-call level; the two projection theorems from the imported-whole level assume HasWitness at a level the benchmark contract excludes by definition and return the transformed-call proof without using that assumption, so they hold vacuously; the benchmark transport shape realizes the six-step shape and is compatible with DP.

There is no witness in the KO7 tower at directWhole and every representable direct orienter fails to orient; kappa of truth lies at or below importedWhole while kappa of the contracted tower lies above importedWhole and at or below transformedCall, jointly as the three-kappa summary.

Unconditionally, both the dependency-pair structural profile and the Godel compiled ascent profile realize the six-step shape; compatibility holds exactly for reflection-family realized profiles with subsingleton comparison hom-sets and witnesses from Godel to DP classical and contentless to Godel; there is a hom from the Godel checker ascent to the quotation ascent with no hom either way between orientation and quotation while all three realize six-step shape; the synthetic all-True Godel profile is stagewise equivalent to DP with reflection family.

openPoints: The external TTT2 FBI run remains MAYBE and is not certifiedYes; internal classification does not upgrade it.

Direction-indexed FBI coverage requires instantiation hypotheses such as forwardOnly, backwardOnly, or matching a direction; unconditional aliases that ignore the direction hypothesis carry no direction-specific content.

The FBI method carrier allows any pairing of instantiation mode and witness constructor with route and status from the witness alone; orientation, direction-witness consistency, and adequacy need additional predicates.

The benchmark conservative extension stores only forward lifts from base to extension with no reverse; its lift ignores the source proof and returns the independently available transformed-call witness.
No cataloged generic DP row uses a direct W0 route; a W0-route claim needs a separate explicit direct certificate.
The synthetic Godel-labelled comparison uses stipulated predicates and shows only stage-shape compatibility with finite-model existentials, leaving model and proof-calculus laws as extra data.

Shape-layer comparison is degenerate with subsingleton hom-sets, but witness-layer morphisms do not transfer: the Godel checker maps to quotation while orientation and quotation admit no morphism either way.

subTopics.name: Six-step ascent comparison and witness order

files.summary: Classifies twelve termination-method families outside the core matrix barriers, each mapping to open, adapter-only, closed or conditional residual status. Provides the finite twelve-element list with nodup, length and completeness lemmas. Proves the status catalog is consistent and exhibits both open and closed members.
files.conclusion: Every one of the twelve additional method families is listed with its assigned residual coverage status, including open and closed cases.

files.summary: Builds structural comparison wrappers above ReflectionSchema with abstract base, obstruction, framework and reimport interfaces. Defines stagewise equivalence to the DP six-step profile and proves transport of realization. Instantiates a synthetic finite Godel-labelled model with stipulated predicates and proves only stage-shape compatibility.
files.conclusion: The synthetic Godel-labelled object is stagewise equivalent to the DP profile and realizes the six-stage ascent shape.

files.summary: This module packages four explicit W1 construction witnesses and records their structural imports. It defines routes, import classes, evidence and success structures. It builds MPO-precedence, nonlinear-polynomial, imported-whole and transparency witnesses, proves each carries its permitted import, and shows imported-whole separation from W0 and escape from additive and affine surfaces.
files.conclusion: Four theorem-backed W1 packages cover precedence, global-polynomial, imported-whole and transparency imports outside W0 direct search.

files.summary: This module defines a finite route-tag catalog with four W1 and two W2 labels. It assigns each label a route tag and an optional W1 import or W2 transform class. It proves the W1 part, the W2 part and their combination, shows every canonical route is non-W0, and records W1 and W2 separation of fullDuplicating from direct search.
files.conclusion: The six canonical W1 and W2 labels have the stated routes and imports or transforms and are all non-W0.

files.summary: This module audits the six canonical construction witnesses. It defines the finite witness list, a payload predicate and an audit catalog abbreviation. It proves every witness appears in the list, every listed witness carries a W1 or W2 payload with non-W0 route, combines these into an audit catalog, and shows any construction certificate implies the audit catalog.
files.conclusion: The six-element inventory is complete with payload and non-W0 route for every row.

files.summary: This module defines a certificate packaging route assignments, payloads, permitted imports and transforms, and full-duplicating separation. It assembles the canonical certificate from component theorems. It proves projections to the route catalog, payload catalog, W1 imports, W2 transforms and fullDuplicating separation.
files.conclusion: The canonical certificate packages routes, payloads, permitted imports and transforms with fullDuplicating separation.

files.summary: This module states exactness for the six-element canonical witness list. It defines a package of duplicate-freedom, length six, membership equivalence, payload presence and non-W0 routes. It proves each component by decide, rewriting or prior audit lemmas and combines them into one exactness catalog.
files.conclusion: The canonical six-element list is duplicate-free, complete, and every row carries payload with non-W0 route.

files.summary: This module partitions the six canonical witnesses into four W1 and two W2 rows. It defines partition predicates and certificate and final-catalog structures. It proves every witness is in exactly one side with matching route and payload, combines certificate with exactness and audit, and bundles everything into a final catalog with projections and agreement lemmas.
files.conclusion: The six witnesses partition into four W1 and two W2 rows with matching routes and payloads in one final catalog.

files.summary: This module attaches proof-bearing success objects to the six canonical labels. It defines optional W1 and W2 adapters and payload-catalog propositions. It proves the W1 and W2 payload catalogs and their combination, extracts permitted imports and transforms, and shows fullDuplicating W1 and W2 payloads separate from direct search.
files.conclusion: All six canonical rows carry payloads with permitted imports or transforms and fullDuplicating stays outside direct search.

files.summary: The file defines forward and backward adequacy data pairing instantiation tags with matching catalog rows. It proves each datum projects to final-catalog coverage and listed closure status, with canonical direct-W0 and imported-W1 fixtures. It assembles the two-row adequacy-boundary catalog and certificate showing universal directional coverage while keeping the external TTT2 FBI run at MAYBE.
files.conclusion: Forward and backward adequacy data always project to final-catalog coverage with no outside-catalog method.

files.summary: The file defines the FBI route, closure-status, and final-catalog taxonomy with finite four-row and twelve-row enumerations. It proves list completeness, that every final row is theorem-backed, and that both the route-status catalog and direction-indexed catalog are total. It keeps the external TTT2 FBI status as MAYBE, disjoint from internal closure statuses.
files.conclusion: The four-row and twelve-row FBI catalogs are complete, supported, and total, with external TTT2 fixed at MAYBE.

files.summary: The file provides a thin import boundary re-exporting the FBI route-status, residual, and adequacy surfaces. It defines four closure rows and proves the closure catalog, final-catalog certificate, and twelve-row direction-indexed catalog with legacy projections. It keeps the external TTT2 FBI result at MAYBE apart from internal classification.
files.conclusion: The final FBI catalog, closure catalog and directional catalog are fully theorem-backed with external TTT2 unchanged at MAYBE.

files.summary: The file defines final-catalog coverage as existence of a declared catalog row matching a method route and closure status, plus a constructor-by-constructor admissibility predicate mirroring FBIComparisonWitness. It proves every witness is admissible and every method has a listed closure status and catalog coverage. It adds direction-indexed coverage theorems that consume the instantiation hypothesis, alongside deprecated aliases that ignore it, and classifies the directional row.
files.conclusion: Every FBI method is covered by a declared final-catalog row with listed closure status, with direction-indexed refinements when the instantiation hypothesis is used.

files.summary: The file defines the FBI method carrier as an instantiation tag paired with a comparison-witness constructor, plus directions, closure statuses and success semantics. Route and closure-status functions classify witnesses by pattern matching independently of instantiation. Four fixtures illustrate direct, imported, transformed-call and certified pairings.
files.conclusion: FBI methods pair an instantiation tag with explicit comparison evidence whose route and closure tags are fixed by constructor, without yet enforcing orientation or adequacy.

files.summary: The file defines a six-constructor exact grammar for DP-style methods and a total four-value status classifier. It proves universal coverage and unconditional classification by finite enumeration. It embeds the four-row boundary catalog into the grammar, proving classification agreement and injectivity.
files.conclusion: Every generic DP method falls in the six-constructor grammar with its fixed status, agreeing with the four-row boundary catalog on the overlap.

files.summary: The file defines a four-row DP boundary carrier with route and status projections and theorem-backed support payloads. It proves every row is supported, the catalog is realized, and no row uses the direct W0 route. It packages the catalog with W0 exclusion and notes subsumption by the six-constructor grammar.
files.conclusion: The four-row DP boundary catalog is realized with theorem-backed support and excludes the direct W0 route.

files.summary: The file fills the six ascent stages with compiled Godel objects: a provable equation, falsum not a Godel sentence, unprovable ConQ, a Q-model refuting ConQ, and unprovable negation of ConQ. It packages a one-step licensed expiry from the issue to ConQ and a corner map to quotation ascent. It proves realization, compatibility and transport to quotation.
files.conclusion: The compiled Godel stages realize the six-step shape and transport by a corner map to quotation ascent.

files.summary: This file defines bare Lawvere-Yanofsky ingredients for code objects, evaluation with self-application, fixed-point-free endomaps and their bundle, alongside finite pair-graph certificates and DP confession structures with optional Lawvere slots. It builds the primitive-duplicator confession with a singleton pair node, well-founded pair problem and external Arts-Giesl license but no internal code, evaluation or fixed-point-free data. It proves this constructed object does not furnish a Lawvere-Yanofsky schema and is semantically separated from that route, with an explicit semantic profile.
files.conclusion: The primitive-duplicator DP confession is a singleton well-founded pair-graph with external license that furnishes no Lawvere-Yanofsky schema.

files.summary: Defines witness languages and one-way conservative extensions as implications between HasWitness propositions, with transport to HasWitness and kappaLe. Instantiates the benchmark projection from imported-whole to transformed-call by ignoring the source and returning the independently available transformed-call witness. Packages this as a reflection-family ascent profile that realizes the six-step shape and is compatible with DP.
files.conclusion: The benchmark imported-whole to transformed-call projection is sound one-way and instantiates a reflection-family ascent profile compatible with DP.

files.summary: The file places the dependency-pair confession profile and the Godel compiled-arithmetic ascent profile under one six-step licensed-ascent shape. It proves both profiles realize the shape, the Godel side with provable arithmetic facts and no stage stipulated True. It proves comparison at the shape layer is degenerate: membership is six true stages plus the reflection tag, any two realized profiles of the same family compare, and hom-sets are subsingletons, with the same degeneracy for LCEL comparison. It then separates layers by showing the Godel checker maps into quotation while orientation and quotation admit no morphism either way, although all three realize the shape and compare at the shape layer.
files.conclusion: Both the dependency-pair and Godel profiles realize the same six-step reflection shape with degenerate comparison, while witness-layer morphisms do not transfer.

files.summary: This file compares six-field proposition-valued structural profiles stage by stage. It defines stage selectors, pointwise realization and equivalence, and a comparison package with transport theorems. It proves realization is equivalent to stagewise realization and that stagewise agreement preserves realization. It derives a stagewise realization and self-comparison for the mechanized dependency-pair profile.
files.conclusion: Pointwise six-stage agreement transports realization of the six-step shape from one profile to another.

files.summary: Defines a three-constructor registry of semantic method classes with route and status metadata and a support predicate linking each class to existing theorems or certificates. Proves every class is supported, the three-member list is exact and complete, and packages the whole catalog and its certificate with the imported method separated from direct W0.
files.conclusion: Every one of the three semantic method classes is supported with its exact route and status, and the imported method is certified as a licensed escape distinct from direct W0.

files.summary: Defines a three-constructor exact grammar for semantic methods and a total classifier assigning every constructor a W1 licensed-escape status. Proves universal coverage and classification, conjoins the six-constructor DP grammar with this three-constructor grammar into a single 9-type universal classification, and embeds the boundary catalog into the grammar injectively.
files.conclusion: All DP plus semantic methods admit universal coverage and classification across exactly nine types, with every semantic method classified as W1 licensed escape.

files.summary: Defines comparison witnesses, historical and grounded comparison objects, and conversions from external classical comparison objects to the grounded interface. Proves stagewise equivalence preserves six-step realization and that any profile compatible with the DP profile, including Godel-1931 and benchmark-transport instances, is structurally identical to the mechanized DP profile.
files.conclusion: Any profile compatible with the DP profile is structurally identical to it, with concrete Godel and benchmark instances theorem-backed.

files.summary: This file defines a two-constructor W2 route class with theorem-bearing evidence and success structures packaging transformed-call witnesses. It proves every W2 success yields a permitted transform and an underlying transformed-call witness, instantiated by canonical duplicating and linear successes. It shows the duplicating W2 route stays separated from direct whole-term search and catalogs both witnesses plus a confession-route agreement conjunction.
files.conclusion: Every theorem-backed W2 success realizes a permitted transformed-call route with an underlying witness, instantiated by canonical duplicating and linear successes separated from direct search.

files.summary: This file defines a three-kind tuple disposition and a decomposition carrying row tags with canonical scalar and matrix observers plus a licensed-escape status witness. It proves every row tag resolves to scalar, matrix, or status. The capstone bundles vector projection identity, matrix-over-polynomial non-orientation, and tuple-row resolution for families with a payload pump.
files.conclusion: Every tuple row resolves to scalar, matrix, or status and the capstone bundles vector projection, matrix reduction, and row resolution.

files.summary: This file inventories two tuple rows with their hypothesis carriers, arity and strict-coordinate projections, and boundary classifiers. It defines a decomposition package requiring scalar components and conditional-barrier status. It proves both rows remain conditional-barrier and every row hypothesis decomposes into scalar observations with its strict coordinate and row-local consequence.
files.conclusion: Every formal tuple row decomposes into finitely many scalar direct-measure observations with a designated strict coordinate and row-local classification.

files.summary: This file states the headline universal dichotomy that every classified first-order interpretation method is W0-blocked or licensed via W1, W2, or external certification. It proves the dichotomy, its verdict-layer form, and carrier exhaustiveness via ten embeddings. It draws tool-search coverage and subsumption of the finite-ledger predecessor plus string audit anchors.
files.conclusion: Every first-order interpretation method is either W0-blocked without unconditional step admission or licensed via W1, W2, or external certification.

files.summary: This file defines Nat-tagged constructor maps for seven blocked families plus W1, W2, and external tags with finite class encodings. It proves each map takes its assigned W0 or licensed verdict by reflexivity. It proves every carrier value matches one constructor family by case split, covering tags outside the finite W1 and W2 images.
files.conclusion: Every carrier value arises from its constructor family with the assigned W0 or licensed verdict.

files.summary: This file defines the ten-constructor method tag type with unrestricted Nat indices and a four-verdict projection. It defines W0-blocked, licensed-via-W1-W2-or-external, and unconditional-admission predicates from the verdict. It proves the verdict dichotomy and the equivalences between blocked, licensed, and admission forms.
files.conclusion: Every method tag is either W0-blocked or licensed, with non-blocked verdicts equivalent to licensed verdicts.

files.summary: This file defines the six propositional slots of the W1 ascent shape parallel to the W2 confession schema. It proves every W1 method-carrier row realizes its ascent profile by carrier lemmas. It proves ascent and confession are structurally exclusive and classifies W1 ascent in the construction family separated from W0 and W2.
files.conclusion: Every W1 carrier row realizes its six-step ascent profile inside the construction family and distinct from W2 confession.

files.summary: This file defines a seven-row W1 catalog with route, import-class, source, status, and support projections backed by canonical, semantic, generic-DP, and FBI surfaces. It proves every row is supported, inventoried without duplication, and separated from W0 and W2. It packages the catalog, permitted-import necessity, and separation into a carrier certificate.
files.conclusion: All seven W1 rows have theorem-backed support, permitted imports, W1 licensed-escape status, and separation from W0 and W2.

files.summary: This file derives verdict-projection corollaries of the imported finite classifier where admission means a non-W0 verdict. It proves admission implies licensing, its contrapositive, the expanded three-verdict form, and the equivalence. It provides a string anchor for the headline theorem.
files.conclusion: Admitting steps unconditionally is equivalent to being licensed via W1, W2, or external certification on the imported carrier.

files.summary: This module separates direct whole-term, imported-whole, and transformed-call witness layers with kappa thresholds and a benchmark contract. It proves no representable direct orienter succeeds while polynomial, MPO, and dependency-pair witnesses populate higher layers. It concludes truth appears at imported-whole but the contract first succeeds at transformed-call.
files.conclusion: Truth first appears at the imported-whole layer while the benchmark contract first becomes satisfiable at the transformed-call layer.

files.summary: This file checks the twelve-family beyond-twelve method catalog and its status function. It verifies the catalog has length twelve without duplicates, is complete and consistent, contains both open and closed families, and assigns canonical statuses such as open for direct pair extraction and closed for the certified external engine. Examples are proved from the status catalog.
files.conclusion: The catalog covers twelve families with both open and closed cases witnessed.

files.summary: This file checks construction routes, W1 import classes, evidence, success predicates and permitted imports. It includes controls exposing permitted imports for MPO, polynomial, imported-whole and transparency cases. It records that fullDuplicating is imported-whole not direct and separated from W0.
files.conclusion: Canonical W1 witnesses each carry their required permitted import with separation from direct search.

files.summary: This file checks the canonical construction certificate, its projections to route, payload, W1 and W2 catalogs, witness completeness and audit implication. It includes two controls for witness membership and for deriving the audit catalog. It proves no new theory beyond exercising the certificate surface.
files.conclusion: The canonical certificate projects correctly and yields a complete audit catalog with non-W0 payloads.

files.summary: This file checks exactness and W1 versus W2 partition for the construction catalog. It checks nodup, length, completeness, payload properties and partition catalogs with consistency. It includes four controls for count six, W1 and W2 membership, and exactness from the certificate.
files.conclusion: Six canonical witnesses partition disjointly into W1 and W2 with payload consistency and exactness.

files.summary: This file checks the final catalog combining certificate, exactness and audit with W1 and W2 characterizations. It checks projections, no-overlap, no-unclassified, payload agreements and per-witness entries. It includes controls enumerating the four W1 and two W2 witnesses with routes and success payloads.
files.conclusion: The final catalog holds four W1 and two W2 witnesses each with matching route and success payload.

files.summary: This file checks W1 and W2 success payload catalogs and their permitted import and transform properties. It checks the route payload catalog and separation of fullDuplicating payloads from direct search. It includes two rfl controls fixing the MPO and fullDuplicating payloads.
files.conclusion: Canonical W1 and W2 payload catalogs hold with correct MPO and fullDuplicating entries.

files.summary: This file checks the base construction route catalog with witness routes and import and transform projections. It checks W1 and W2 route catalogs and non-W0 properties with fullDuplicating separation. It includes two controls that imported-whole and fullDuplicating routes differ from W0.
files.conclusion: Imported-whole and fullDuplicating canonical routes are non-W0.

files.summary: This file reach-checks the FBI adequacy-boundary layer, including forward and backward adequacy data, canonical fixtures, final coverage, closure statuses, catalogs and certificates, plus direction-indexed route data and external TTT2 status, with #check and #print axioms. It provides fifteen examples projecting final coverage, instantiation directions, listed closure statuses, catalog data existence, routes W0 and W1, boundary statuses and directional coverage. It proves no new theory beyond these projections.
files.conclusion: All adequacy-boundary and directional-route names type-check and the canonical fixtures project the stated coverage, routes and statuses.

files.summary: This file reach-checks the FBI classification layer, including directions, instantiations, witnesses, closure statuses, final catalog rows, residual boundaries, certificates and fixtures, plus directional rows and external tool status, with #check and #print axioms. It provides twelve examples for routes W0, W1 and W2, closure statuses, catalog support, boundary instantiations and the twelve-row directional count. It proves no new theory beyond these checks.
files.conclusion: All FBI classification, catalog and directional names type-check and the fixtures project the stated routes, statuses and twelve-row count.

files.summary: This file reach-checks the FBI final-catalog layer, including route-status, residual-boundary, adequacy-boundary and closure catalogs, certificates, and the direction-indexed catalog API with external tool status. It provides eight projection examples for coverage, routes and universal method coverage, plus two certificate examples pinning the twelve-row count and MAYBE external status. It proves no new theory beyond these checks.
files.conclusion: The final catalog, closure catalog and directional certificate type-check with twelve rows and external TTT2 status MAYBE.

files.summary: This file is a root reach gate that reaches the FBI final catalog through ResidualMethodAPI rather than the catalog module directly. It checks the live catalog surface, the direction-indexed route and status catalog with coverage theorems and certificates, and the MAYBE external TTT2 status, with #check and #print axioms. It provides five examples projecting certificate fields and the twelve-row count.
files.conclusion: The final catalog is reachable through the integrated root with twelve directional rows and MAYBE external status.

files.summary: This file reach-checks generic FBI adequacy, including admissible witnesses, forward and backward adequacy classes, universal unconditional theorems and direction-indexed coverage. It provides nine examples instantiating admissibility, adequacy classes and directional coverage on the direct, imported and transformed fixtures. It prints axioms for the new directional anchors and proves no new theory.
files.conclusion: Forward, backward and direction-indexed generic adequacy coverage type-check and hold on the direct, imported and transformed fixtures.

files.summary: This reach gate checks the generic-DP and semantic method boundary catalogs, including support, status and route projections and explicit certificate requirements. Examples verify that transformedCallRoute is supported, importedOrdering is a W1 licensed escape, certifiedEngine is never W0, and parallel semantic facts including a direct witness for fullLinear. It contains only checks of catalog types with no new definitions.
files.conclusion: Transformed and transparent methods are supported while imported orderings and model imports are W1 licensed escapes, never W0.

files.summary: This reach test confirms the public surface of the generic-DP and semantic-method grammars for Lane D. It checks canonical enumerations, total classification, universal coverage D.3 and D.4 and the combined D.7 conjunction. It also checks that the boundary catalogs embed into the exact grammars with classification agreement.
files.conclusion: Both grammars are universally covering and totally classified, with nine total methods and exact boundary-to-grammar agreement.

files.summary: This file checks the transformed-call classification surface. It verifies transform classes, evidence, permitted transforms, the requirement that success needs a permitted transform and witness, fullDuplicating and fullLinear successes, separation from direct search, confession-route projection, and the witness catalog. Its three examples confirm a transformed witness, absence of a direct witness, and route-evidence equality.
files.conclusion: FullDuplicating succeeds through a permitted transformed call without any direct witness.

files.summary: This file is an elaboration check for the tuple-interpretation decomposition module. It checks carriers and classifiers, hypothesis projections, the scalar-component surface, the decomposition package, constructors and theorems, with an axiom print for the unconditional decomposition. It declares no new examples or theorems of its own.
files.conclusion: Every tuple-interpretation row decomposes into scalar components with unconditional decomposition despite conditional barrier status.

files.summary: The file imports the universal first-order interpretation-method, embeddings, dichotomy and W1/W2-necessity modules and defines no new theory. It runs `#check` on interpretation methods, verdicts, licensing predicates, embedding families and anchor constants to expose their types. It adds example terms that instantiate the unconditional dichotomy, W0-blocked embeddings, W1/W2 licensing necessity, residual verdict coverage and anchor-string equalities.
files.conclusion: Every universal first-order interpretation method is either W0-blocked or licensed via W1, W2 or external certification, with unconditional step admission coinciding with licensing.

files.summary: This file checks the W1 ascent structural identity theory. It verifies the six-step profile, realization predicate, slots, profile function, headline identity theorem, distinctness from W2 confession, and family classification. Eight examples assert that every W1 row realizes its profile, that four canonical rows do so, that construction and confession cannot share rank, and both parts of the classification.
files.conclusion: Every W1 method row realizes its six-step ascent profile, and no construction response shares rank with a forgetting witness.

files.summary: This file checks the W1 method carrier catalog. It verifies row and status types, route and import and source projections, support predicates, nodup and length and completeness lemmas, exact projection equations, catalog certificate with its projections, separation from W0 and W2, and projections to semantic, generic-DP and FBI boundaries. Ten examples instantiate the catalog, support, permitted import, route and status equations, boundary projections, import-class equation, and separation.
files.conclusion: The W1 carrier catalog is exact and projects to support, route, status, necessity and separation from W0 and W2.
